claims: C1 models should honor user requests
C2 honoring a user request is not required when the request conflicts with a developer-level instruction
C3 honoring a user request is not required when the request conflicts with a system-level instruction
C4 honoring a user request is not required when the request conflicts with a root-level instruction

concepts.name: user_authority
concepts.gloss: R is a request made by an end user, carrying the user level of instruction authority

concepts.name: authority_levels_hierarchy
concepts.gloss: the ranking of instruction authority levels, root > system > developer > user > guideline > no authority, used to determine which instruction prevails in conflicts

concepts.name: user_request
concepts.gloss: R is a request from an end user that the model is being asked to honor

concepts.name: developer_instruction
concepts.gloss: I is an instruction issued at the developer level of authority

concepts.name: system_instruction
concepts.gloss: I is an instruction issued at the system level of authority

concepts.name: root_instruction
concepts.gloss: I is an instruction issued at the root level of authority

concepts.name: conflicts_with
concepts.gloss: request R conflicts with instruction I, meaning honoring R would contradict what I directs
concepts.inference: the clause's 'unless they conflict with' requires a relation between a request and an instruction that contradicts it

ontology.gloss: R is a request from an end user

asserts.read_back: honoring user request % is not required because it conflicts with developer-level instruction %
honoring user request % is not required because it conflicts with system-level instruction %
honoring user request % is not required because it conflicts with root-level instruction %

closure.reason: the clause obliges honoring user requests only when they do not conflict with higher-level instructions; it does not forbid declining a request that conflicts, so silence permits not honoring in that case
